title: Keep ordinary checkpoint receipt effects recoverable across the first Accepted persistence cut
outcome: An ordinary owned checkpoint cannot become durably Accepted/Confirmed and unrecoverably skip its verification and pending-batch receipt effects after restart; preserve exact receipt custody, successor ownership and acknowledgement boundaries.
acceptance: The first durable owned ordinary Checkpointed cut includes the exact verification and pending-batch effects, or durable replay custody sufficient for a fresh host to finish them without another checkpoint or provider invocation.

A real SQLite cut after first Accepted persistence and before local acknowledgement, followed by a new AppState, proves the exact canonical receipt and non-vacuous evidence associations and batch targets are retained and applied once; no unresolved independent duty is released.

Failed persistence and non-owning or successor-drift results preserve canonical receipt custody without mutating the successor, bypassing current authority, or acknowledging effects absent from the durable cut.
